outcome: Nothing has settled or moved the characteristic-zero question since 26 January 2024. The only in-window item bearing on it is a 2025 preprint (Johnson, Tran, Walsberg, Ye) that answers an unrelated question of Lampe and, per a search excerpt I could not confirm in the text I could open, makes a Podewski counterexample depend on an open topology question (Question 11.1). The 2026 AI-assisted counterexample found by the AI search concerns the stable forking conjecture, not this problem.
problem_asks: One question, about the characteristic-zero case. (1) Let K be an infinite field that is minimal: every subset of K definable in the field language is finite or cofinite. The bullet says every definable subset of the structure without saying 'with parameters' or naming the language; the literature (Podewski's conjecture) uses the pure field language with parameters, and I have recorded that reading. (2) Restrict to characteristic zero. The positive-characteristic case is settled by Wagner (JSL 2000), but it is not what the bullet asks. (3) Asked: is every such K algebraically closed? A yes answers the bullet positively. A no needs an infinite minimal field of characteristic zero that is not algebraically closed. Nothing else is asked.

events.what_happened: Frank O. Wagner, 'Minimal fields', Journal of Symbolic Logic 65(4), pp. 1833-1835 (print issue December 2000; Cambridge lists online publication 12 March 2014). Abstract, verbatim as I read it on the Cambridge page: 'A minimal field of non-zero characteristic is algebraically closed.' This settles the positive-characteristic case of Podewski's conjecture only. Wagner's publication list (opened) also gives a 1999 proceedings paper with the same title ('Minimal fields', Kobe, Tokai University) and 'Minimal fields and bad fields in non-zero characteristic' (1999, Erlagol); I did not open those, so the first written argument may predate 2000.
events.revisions: Cambridge gives online publication 12 March 2014 and print December 2000. The 1999 proceedings titles on Wagner's publication list may be earlier write-ups; not opened.
events.delivers: Every minimal field of non-zero characteristic is algebraically closed. Restricted to positive characteristic. Says nothing about characteristic zero.
events.remains: The whole characteristic-zero question: whether every infinite minimal field of characteristic zero is algebraically closed.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of the Association for Symbolic Logic)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result; refereed

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, in positive characteristic only, where it proves it. No bearing on characteristic zero.

events.what_happened: Krzysztof Krupinski, Predrag Tanovic, Frank O. Wagner, 'Around Podewski's conjecture', arXiv:1201.5709 (v1 27 January 2012; v2 28 August 2012); Fundamenta Mathematicae 222 (2013) 175-193, DOI 10.4064/fm222-2-4. Abstract: 'We reduce Podewski's conjecture to the (partially) ordered case.' Main statements as I read them in the full PDF: Theorem 1, 'A minimal unordered field is algebraically closed.'; Conjecture 2, 'There is no minimal ordered field of characteristic zero.'; Theorem 3, 'There is no almost linear minimal field.' Here almost linear means incomparability is transitive. The paper also treats minimal groups, including an almost linear minimal group of exponent 2 (a group, not a field). The abstract says the conjecture 'remains wide open in the zero-characteristic case' and the introduction says 'the characteristic zero case remains one of the oldest unsolved problems in algebraic model theory'. The paper's bibliography dates the prediction to Podewski's work of 1973.
events.revisions: v1 27 Jan 2012; v2 28 Aug 2012; published Fundamenta Mathematicae 222 (2013).
events.delivers: (a) Every minimal field that is unordered, in the paper's sense, is algebraically closed (Theorem 1 as I read it; the excerpt I read states no characteristic hypothesis). (b) There is no almost linear minimal field (Theorem 3). Together with the reduction, the characteristic-zero problem is reduced to minimal ordered fields. Not a resolution of characteristic zero.
events.remains: Characteristic zero, ordered case: every minimal ordered field of characteristic zero (Conjecture 2 of the paper, which the paper leaves open). This includes minimal fields with a definable well partial order with an infinite chain, which the paper conjectures do not exist, and minimal ordered fields that are not almost linear.

checked_by.who: Fundamenta Mathematicae (journal of the Institute of Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper as Fund. Math. 222 (2013) 175-193

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture. Proves it for unordered minimal fields and for the almost linear ordered case; conjectures that the remaining ordered characteristic-zero case is empty. No counterexample.
events.object: No counterexample to the field question. The paper's exhibited object is an almost linear minimal group (M,<,+,0) of exponent 2 (a group, not a field), which is not an object for the field question.

events.what_happened: Kenji Fukuzaki, 'On minimal fields', RIMS Kokyuroku 1390 (2004), pp. 30-33, from a meeting on generic structures. I could not read the PDF (binary through my fetch tool), so this rests on search excerpts of the paper. Per those excerpts: Section 1 is titled 'Minimal fields with infinite bases'; a minimal structure with an infinite basis is strongly minimal, so a minimal field with an infinite basis is algebraically closed; the paper also gives a direct proof of the lemma 'a minimal field K with an infinite basis is algebraically closed', and states that the treatment covers all characteristics.
events.delivers: Minimal fields with an infinite basis are algebraically closed, in the paper's sense of 'basis', which I could not check. If the result covers characteristic zero as the excerpts say, it settles characteristic zero only for minimal fields with an infinite basis.
events.remains: Minimal fields of characteristic zero without an infinite basis (in the paper's sense), so the general characteristic-zero question.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, as a partial result under the basis hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Tomasz Gogacz and Krzysztof Krupinski, 'On regular groups and fields', arXiv:1211.3852 (submitted 16 November 2012, v1 only); Journal of Symbolic Logic (2014) per search metadata. The arXiv abstract page (opened) says the conjectures that minimal or quasi-minimal fields are algebraically closed have a common generalization, the conjecture that each regular field is algebraically closed. It also states 'Standard arguments show that a generically stable regular field is algebraically closed.' Search excerpts (not opened) add that the non-generically-stable case is open and that the authors show unbounded orbits for powers of the global generic type.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; journal version JSL 2014 per search metadata (not opened).
events.delivers: Does not settle minimal fields. Proves that a generically stable regular field is algebraically closed. Minimal fields are regular, so the general conjecture would cover Podewski's conjecture, but whether minimal fields of characteristic zero are generically stable is not established by anything I read.
events.remains: The minimal-field case in general, in characteristic zero; the non-generically-stable case.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2014), per search metadata; not opened

events.direction: Partial and general: generalizes the problem to regular fields; proves the generically stable case. Does not cut either way on minimal fields.

events.what_happened: Krzysztof Krupinski, 'Superrosy fields and valuations', arXiv:1308.3394 (single version, submitted 15 August 2013), math.LO with cross-list math.AC. The abstract as I read it: 'We also notice that minimal fields have the property that every non-trivial valuation has divisible value group'; and 'In the zero characteristic case, we get some partial results of this kind.' The main positive statement in the abstract is for positive characteristic and includes an algebraically closed residue field.
events.delivers: A structural fact about valuations on minimal fields: every non-trivial valuation has divisible value group. Characteristic-zero results are described only as partial. Does not establish algebraic closedness of minimal fields.
events.direction: Neither way. A property of minimal fields, with no verdict on algebraic closedness.

events.what_happened: Lior Bary-Soroker and Arno Fehm, 'Open Problems in the Theory of Ample Fields', arXiv:1106.1310 (submitted 7 June 2011); a survey. Its Question V asks whether every radically closed field is ample. Per survey excerpts found through search (I opened only the arXiv abstract page), Koenigsmann observed that a positive answer to Question V would imply Podewski's conjecture, because minimal fields are radically closed and an ample minimal field must be algebraically closed. The survey notes that the conjecture is proved only for positive characteristic, citing Wagner's paper.
events.delivers: Not a result on minimal fields. It is a reduction: a positive answer to Question V (every radically closed field is ample) would imply Podewski's conjecture in all characteristics. Question V itself is not answered here.
events.remains: Everything, including Question V on which the reduction depends.
events.direction: None on the problem itself. Conditionally points toward the conjecture, if Question V has a positive answer.
people: Jochen Koenigsmann (observation credited in the survey)

events.what_happened: Will Johnson, Chieu-Minh Tran, Erik Walsberg, Jinhe Ye, 'Large implies henselian', arXiv:2508.10886 (v1 14 August 2025; v2 7 March 2026), math.LO and math.AG. Opened: the arXiv abstract and the introduction (Section 1). The paper gives a characterization of large fields and introduces a finite-closed topology on V(K). Its abstract says 'we construct several examples where these two differ, which allows us to answer a question of Lampe'. Lampe's question (MathOverflow 2009, per the introduction and search excerpts of the Jarden paper) asks whether there is an infinite field K and a polynomial h with K minus h(K) nonempty and finite. Per a search excerpt of Theorem D (not opened), there is a bounded PAC field K with a quintic polynomial h such that h(K) is K minus {0}. Introduction (opened): 'We could not determine whether there is an infinite perfect field K on which the finite-closed topology is discrete', and this 'is related to important open problems in field theory; see Section 11.' Per a search excerpt of Section 11 (not opened; sections 10-11 were unreadable through my tool), Question 11.1 asks this question, the paper observes that a counterexample to Podewski's conjecture would force the topology to be discrete, and so a negative answer to Question 11.1 in characteristic zero would prove Podewski's conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 14 Aug 2025 (58 KB); v2 7 Mar 2026 (45 KB). I did not compare versions.
events.delivers: Relative to the problem: no minimal-field result. On Lampe's question: examples exist (search excerpt: a bounded PAC field, not Hilbertian by the excerpted discussion). On Podewski, per the search excerpt: it poses Question 11.1 and makes a negative answer to Question 11.1 in characteristic zero sufficient for the conjecture. It does not establish Question 11.1 and does not answer the bullet.
events.remains: The characteristic-zero Podewski question, and Question 11.1 itself, which by the paper's own Section 1 wording is open.
events.direction: Relative to the bullet: none directly. The Lampe example (per excerpt) is a polynomial whose image is cofinite, which is the shape a minimal non-closed field would need for a polynomial image. Nothing I read shows the example field is minimal; this is my observation, not the paper's claim. The Podewski link is conditional on Question 11.1.
events.object: Per a search excerpt of Theorem D, not opened: a bounded PAC field K and a quintic polynomial map h over K whose image is K minus {0}. Whether the example is explicit or non-constructive, and its characteristic, were not established by my reading.

events.what_happened: James Freitag and Scott Mutchnik, 'A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture', arXiv:2609.00436 (single version; submitted 31 August 2026). Opened: the arXiv abstract page. Abstract sentence: 'Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture.' The arXiv page mentions neither minimal fields nor Podewski's conjecture. A secondary news article (aiweekly, opened) says the conjecture is Hart, Kim and Pillay's (1996) and that the authors wrote the proofs without AI. That statement is not on the arXiv page I opened, so I do not rely on it.
events.delivers: A claimed counterexample to the stable forking conjecture, a conjecture in stability theory. Nothing about minimal fields or the characteristic-zero Podewski question. Discarded as a result on a neighbouring problem. The Wikipedia list has a separate bullet, 'Stable forking conjecture for simple theories', which is not this bullet.
events.direction: Cuts against the stable forking conjecture if the claim holds. Irrelevant to minimal fields.
events.object: A claimed counterexample to the stable forking conjecture. I read only the abstract page, so I cannot say what the object is.

summary: The bullet is Podewski's conjecture. Wikipedia's bullet carries no hyperlink, so it points nowhere. From the sources I opened: Wagner (JSL 2000) proved the positive-characteristic case. Krupinski, Tanovic and Wagner (arXiv 2012; Fund. Math. 2013) prove that an unordered minimal field is algebraically closed (Theorem 1) and that no almost linear minimal field exists (Theorem 3). They reduce the rest to minimal ordered fields and conjecture that no minimal ordered field of characteristic zero exists (Conjecture 2). The paper calls the characteristic-zero case 'one of the oldest unsolved problems in algebraic model theory'. Fukuzaki (RIMS Kokyuroku 1390, 2004) reports that a minimal field with an infinite basis is algebraically closed; I could not read the PDF, so this rests on search excerpts. Gogacz and Krupinski (arXiv 2012) place the problem under the conjecture that every regular field is algebraically closed, and prove the generically stable case. Krupinski (arXiv 2013) gives valuation facts about minimal fields, with only partial characteristic-zero results. Nothing in the window since 26 January 2024 moves the characteristic-zero question as the bullet asks it. The one in-window item bearing on it is Johnson, Tran, Walsberg and Ye (arXiv 2508.10886, v1 August 2025, v2 March 2026). It answers a 2009 MathOverflow question of Lampe about polynomial images with a finite nonempty complement. I opened its introduction, which says the authors 'could not determine whether there is an infinite perfect field K on which the finite-closed topology is discrete'. A search excerpt says the paper shows a Podewski counterexample would force that topology to be discrete, so a negative answer to Question 11.1 in characteristic zero would prove the conjecture. I could not open sections 10 and 11 to confirm this, so the link is unverified. Nothing I found answers Question 11.1. Close calls: (a) Theorem 1 of the 2012 paper is quoted in what I read without a characteristic hypothesis, so it may already cover unordered characteristic-zero fields; the judging pass should check the paper's standing hypotheses. (b) The 2025 paper's result is on Lampe's question and a topology, not on minimal fields; its link to Podewski runs through Question 11.1, which stays open. (c) Fukuzaki's infinite-basis result reaches characteristic zero only if 'basis' means what I assume, which I could not check. (d) The Lampe example, as a search excerpt summarises it, is a bounded PAC field whose polynomial image is K minus {0}. That cofinite-image shape is what a minimal non-closed field would need, but nothing I read shows the example is minimal; this is my observation, not the paper's claim. The AI search found no AI system credited with anything on this problem. It surfaced the OpenAI unit-distance announcement (May 2026), the OpenAI Astra results (August 2026), DeepMind's Aletheia work (2026), Epoch's FrontierMath open-problems track, and the Freitag-Mutchnik preprint on stable forking, which credits ChatGPT 5.6. None of these concerns minimal fields in the sources I looked at. Wagner's BIRS neostability reports (2015, 2018), which a search excerpt says list this problem as open, were unreadable PDFs, so I do not use them. The 2010 FOM posts returned 404.
competing_reading: The problem is largely reduced rather than open. On this reading, Theorem 1 of Krupinski, Tanovic and Wagner (unordered minimal fields are algebraically closed), together with Fukuzaki's infinite-basis result, covers most of characteristic zero, leaving only the ordered case, so the bullet is partly resolved. The opposing reading is that a reduction is not a settled case, so the bullet remains open with its remaining ordered and finite-basis cases. The record does not decide between these; the judging pass must.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The 2012 paper's standing assumptions and the exact scope of Theorem 1, including its characteristic hypothesis and what 'ordered' excludes. (2) Fukuzaki 2004: the definition of 'basis' and the characteristic hypothesis. (3) Johnson, Tran, Walsberg and Ye, Sections 10 and 11 and Theorem D: the wording of Question 11.1, the Podewski remark, the characteristic of the Lampe example, and whether that example can be minimal. (4) A search of arXiv math.LO for 2024-2026 papers mentioning 'Podewski' or 'minimal field', which I could only approximate through a general web index. (5) Whether the 2026 Freitag-Mutchnik preprint says anything about minimal or ordered fields; I read only its abstract page.

judgement.why: The statement asks only about characteristic zero, so Wagner's positive-characteristic theorem is a variant, not a case. Krupinski-Tanovic-Wagner (unordered minimal fields), Fukuzaki (infinite basis) and Gogacz-Krupinski (generically stable regular fields) each settle a class of objects and are cases, all before the snapshot; none resolves the question, and the record itself quotes KTW calling characteristic zero wide open. The only in-window items are Johnson-Tran-Walsberg-Ye, which at most reduces Podewski to an open topology question (none), and Freitag-Mutchnik, which is about the stable forking conjecture, a different problem (variant). Its AI role is answered from its own abstract quote as assisted rather than generated because a news report says the humans wrote the proofs; it is discarded either way.
judgement.doubts: Gogacz-Krupinski as a 'case' is a close call: it proves a generalized conjecture for generically stable regular fields, and it is not established which minimal fields of characteristic zero fall under that; it could be read as variant. No effect on status since it predates the snapshot and is not whole. In-window arXiv coverage was approximated via a general web index.
